Triage: **the deciding fact has been taken from the cloud repo** (in this triage session's authorization surface), so this is queueable now, not a decision card. ⇒ `domain:cli` (the doc records the CLI's `resolveConsolePath()` surface), type `Task`, → `pm:queue`.

**Reading (cloud @ `b7d3dafe`): the code side is current, the README is stale.** Cloud's production overlay targets `@objectstack/console`, not the `@object-ui/console` npm package:
- `apps/cloud/Dockerfile` and `apps/objectos/Dockerfile` both carry the operative comment: "Framework's CLI resolveConsolePath() looks for `@objectstack/console` only — the legacy `@object-ui/console` fallback was removed …", and overlay into `objectstack/packages/console/dist` (the workspace location of `@objectstack/console`).
- `apps/cloud/scripts/extract-console-assets.mjs` states the overlay as "overlay @objectstack/console → /repo/objectstack/packages/console/dist".
- `scripts/dev-local/verify-console-pin.mjs` asserts the overlaid path at `apps/objectos/node_modules/@objectstack/console/dist`; `run-stack.sh` / `README.md` describe the same.

So the fix here is the README correction: `packages/console/README.md:27-31` should describe the actual resolution (`@objectstack/console` only; `@object-ui/console` survives solely as the sibling-repo **source-checkout** dev probe in step 3, matching a workspace `package.json` name — not a `node_modules` resolution), and drop the false "so cloud's Docker overlay keeps working" consequence.

Serial note: #10921's in-flight PR edits this same README (different defect class). Land after #10921 and re-verify line anchors on the merged ref. `Size/model suggestion:` S doc-only, sonnet.

Cross-repo residue: cloud's own prose still carries the stale claim in two places (`AGENTS.md` 发版操作 bullet: "`cp -r` 覆盖到 framework `node_modules/@object-ui/{console,studio}` … static plugin 用 `require.resolve('@object-ui/...')`", and the stale header paragraphs at the top of both Dockerfiles that contradict their own later operative comments). Filed separately in the cloud repo (see back-link comment there) — not this card's surface.

- **Container & model**: S doc-only, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`. ⚠️ Triage suggested `sonnet`; **not adopted, with a reason** — the correct text turns on a distinction that is easy to flatten (`@object-ui/console` survives as a *source-checkout name match*, ⛔ not as a `node_modules` resolution), and getting that half-right produces a doc that is still false.
- **Clause-②**: no — README prose only; no code, no contract, no public surface.
- **Serial constraints cleared**: triage placed this behind **#10921's in-flight PR on this same README**. **#10921 closed `completed` at 08:07:08Z (PR #11266 MERGED)** — serial released, ~8 minutes before this dispatch. ⚠️ #11266 edited **both** files in this card's surface, so ⛔ every line anchor in the card and in triage's note is stale.

## Premise re-verified on the merged ref — and it survived

Triage said to re-verify anchors after #10921. Done at `origin/main` post-#11266; the defect is **intact and unabsorbed**:

```
packages/console/README.md:33  falls back to `@object-ui/console` when present — so cloud's Docker
packages/console/README.md:34  overlay (which `cp -r`s its build over `node_modules/@object-ui/console`)
packages/console/README.md:35  keeps working.
```

⇒ Triage's cited anchor `:27-31` is now **`:31-35`**. Re-derive it again at your head.

## Fix direction — measured, so you do not have to guess which side is stale

The card says the README and `console.ts` "say the opposite." I checked which one is wrong rather than leaving you to decide:

```
packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:48   const CONSOLE_PACKAGE = '@objectstack/console';
packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:28   NOTE: the legacy `@object-ui/console` npm package was the upstream
packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:31   installs both target `@objectstack/console` exclusively now.
packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:242  (pkg.name === CONSOLE_PACKAGE || pkg.name === '@object-ui/console') &&
```

⇒ **The code is current; the README is stale.** There is no `node_modules` fallback to `@object-ui/console`. Line 242's mention is inside **step 3, the sibling-repo dev probe** (`../objectui/apps/console`) — it matches a *workspace `package.json` name* on a source checkout. Two consequences for the text:

1. The sentence "falls back to `@object-ui/console` when present" is wrong as a description of npm resolution.
2. The trailing consequence — "so cloud's Docker overlay keeps working" — is **false and load-bearing**, and is the more dangerous half: cloud's overlay targets `@objectstack/console` (its own Dockerfiles say so). Leaving that sentence tells an operator the overlay works by a mechanism that no longer exists.

⛔ Do not "fix" this by adding the fallback back to the code. The removal was deliberate.

## ⛔ Out of scope

- `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` — **read-only**. If you find the code genuinely wrong, stop and report; ⛔ do not edit it under a docs card.
- Cloud's own stale prose (its `AGENTS.md` release bullet and both Dockerfile header paragraphs) — triage already filed that in the `cloud` repo. ⛔ Not this surface, and not this repo.
- The `@object-ui/console` rows in the comparison table at `:23-27` and the `Updating` steps at `:43,47` — those describe the **objectui package and build**, which genuinely exist. ⛔ Do not sweep them out just because they match the same string.

## Required of the report

`gates` / `deviations` / `files_changed`, plus the re-derived line anchors you actually edited. ⛔ Do not restate the PR body. Docs-only in a published package — decide `skip-changeset` vs a real changeset from the repo's own rule and state which and why.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #11281

Reviewer of record: `domain:cli` seat, session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`. Checked **against GitHub and the tree**, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### Checklist conclusion

| item | verdict |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✅, base `main` ✅, `Fixes #11262` ✅ |
| Changed files | **exactly 2** — `packages/console/README.md`, `.changeset/console-readme-resolution-order.md`. Read from the diff, not the report |
| Read-only fence honoured | `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` — **0 bytes in the diff** ✅ |
| Exclusion list honoured | comparison-table row `:29` and the `Updating` steps sit **outside the hunk** ✅ — the diff physically cannot have swept them |
| ACCEPT path fork | path面 clean — no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. ⇒ ordinary landing, not the governed hold |
| Clause-② | no — prose only, no contract surface, no public widening |

### The part that actually mattered: is the new text *true*?

For a docs-accuracy card, "did it edit the right lines" is the cheap half. I checked each claim the new prose makes against `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` myself:

- *"resolves `@objectstack/console` and nothing else … both require the resolved `package.json` to be named `@objectstack/console`"* → matches `CONSOLE_PACKAGE = '@objectstack/console'` (`:48`) and the function's own header note (`:28-31`). ✅
- *"`@object-ui/console` survives in exactly one place: the sibling-repo dev fallback … a **source** tree at `../objectui/apps/console`"* → matches the dual-name check at `:242`, which sits inside the step-3 source probe. ✅ **This is the distinction I flagged as the easy one to flatten, and it did not get flattened** — the corrected text keeps source-checkout probe and package resolution explicitly apart.
- *"Cloud and objectos Docker images overlay … into `@objectstack/console`'s `dist/`"* → matches triage's cloud reading (`b7d3dafe`). The false "so cloud's Docker overlay keeps working" consequence — the load-bearing half — is gone. ✅

### Changeset — warrant verified independently, ⛔ not taken on the report's word

The dev argued a real changeset (patch, `@objectstack/console`) rather than `skip-changeset`, on the grounds that the README ships to npm. I checked the premise rather than the conclusion:

```
packages/console/package.json → files: ['dist', 'README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md']
```

✅ The prose genuinely is the page npm renders, so `skip-changeset` would have been **wrong** here. Reasoned from the repo's own rule and precedent, which is what the dispatch asked for instead of a default.

### One judgment I am endorsing rather than overriding

The dev left the table's `Use` cell (`:29`, *"Cloud overlays…"* under the `@object-ui/console` column) alone and said why: cloud does build its overlay **content** from the objectui side, and only the overlay **target** is `@objectstack/console`. That reading is correct and it was inside the exclusion list anyway. ⭐ Recording it because a less careful pass would have "fixed" that cell and made the table wrong in the other direction.

### Deviation, examined and accepted

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` not run — but **discharged by measurement rather than merely declared**: this diff contributes zero files to eslint's population (`.md` matches no `files:` block in `eslint.config.mjs`; `--format json` reports 2 results / 0 non-ignored / 0 errors), and `eslint.config.mjs` is not in the diff, so no untouched file's config changes either. That is the right shape for a narrowing — it measures the thing rather than asserting it is fine.

### Landing — ⛔ NOT enqueued yet, on purpose

CI at `c26f8957` shows **zero failures**, but **`Lint & Repo Gates` is still `in_progress`** — and that is the job carrying this diff's gate families. Per the standing rule, release is judged on the **named gate job reaching `completed: success`**, ⛔ never on an aggregate "nothing red yet" reading. `in_progress` is an honest reading, not a pass.

⇒ Flip to ready + arm SQUASH once that job and the remaining shards converge green, then **read back that the arm actually took** — measured on #11252 an hour ago, an arm that silently does not stick leaves the PR sitting `clean` + unmerged forever.

## ✅ Landing audit — PR #11281 MERGED as `cebef551`

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`.

### Two independent readings

1. `origin/main` carries `cebef551 docs(console): README describes the real Console resolution, not a removed npm fallback (#11262) (#11281)`.
2. Probe measured **in both directions plus a control**, so it can fail three distinct ways rather than merely confirm presence:

| probe | want | on `origin/main` |
|---|---|---|
| removed: ``falls back to `@object-ui/console` when present`` | 0 | **0** ✅ |
| removed: ``cp -r`s its build over`` | 0 | **0** ✅ |
| added: `there is **no**` | 1 | **1** ✅ |
| added: `source-checkout probe` | 1 | **1** ✅ |
| **control** — table row `Standalone Console SPA on its own release cadence`, which the exclusion list said must survive | 1 | **1** ✅ |

⭐ The control row is the one that makes this audit worth more than a presence check: it confirms the dispatch's **exclusion list held all the way through the merge**, not just at review time. A sweep that had over-corrected the comparison table would have passed every other row above.

### What landed

The README now states the real resolution order — `@objectstack/console` only via npm, with `@object-ui/console` surviving solely as the sibling-repo **source-checkout** dev probe — and the false *"so cloud's Docker overlay keeps working"* consequence is gone, replaced with the actual overlay target. ⛔ `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` was never touched; the fallback removal it documents stays removed.

⛔ Nothing was landed by weakening anything: no gate bypassed, no test skipped, no queue circumvented.

### One note for the record

This PR was **ejected from the merge queue once** on an unrelated infrastructure failure — Corepack's pnpm download crashing Node's bundled undici parser (`assert(!this.paused)`), filed as **#11300**. It was re-queued once on the "died before any test body ran" ground and merged on the second pass. ⛔ No commit was pushed for that ejection and nothing about this diff changed; recording it so the two queue attempts do not read as two review cycles.

Card closed by the merge.
